source_snapshot.procedure:
【Before Test】
    1. Check that the SUT configuration (e.g., hardware, firmware, drivers, etc.) matches the specifications/recipe definition.
    2. Clear logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.).

    【During Test】
    Use tool to check PCH security
1. Boot into Bios.
2. .Use tool to check  BIOS security status ..

    【After Test】
    1. Collect test results and photos, and save them to specific folders.
    2. Check if there are unexpected logs (e.g., dmesg, syslog, SEL, etc.) generate after test.
source_snapshot.criteria: 1. Make sure the status is pass.

historical_reviews.deepseek: PARTIAL; identifies the vendor-tool dependency but does not constrain the operation to read-only or define the fuse/security target and PASS schema.
historical_reviews.gpt_v2: REQUIRES PACKAGE / USER CONFIRMATION / CHANGED; adds exact PCH identity, signed read-only tool, BIOS/KVM evidence and a prohibition on fuse programming.
historical_reviews.round_02: No separate exact-code round-02 entry was found.
historical_reviews.second_review_handoff: Confirms an operator-facing BIOS/vendor security-status check and the need to stop if write behavior is possible.

original_test_intent: Inspect the intended PCH hardware-security fuse state in the BIOS environment with the owner-approved diagnostic and determine whether the identified target's decoded status satisfies the platform security specification, without changing any fuse.
original_method: A qualified operator enters the specified BIOS/diagnostic context, confirms the exact board/PCH target and read-only mode, invokes the vendor security/fuse status tool, records the full decoded output and BIOS/KVM evidence, and supplies it for comparison with the authoritative PASS definition.
manual_activity: The source places the core check inside BIOS and requires observation of a vendor security-status display. A qualified operator must enter that environment, select the exact target/tool mode and attest the displayed output. The agent may validate inputs and analyze captured evidence but must not claim the BIOS interaction or visual observation.
required_inputs: Exact motherboard, chipset/PCH stepping and intended fuse/security field set
Signed vendor diagnostic, version/hash, compatibility and explicit read-only operating instructions
Authoritative decoded status schema and PASS values for this platform
Qualified BIOS/KVM operator, maintenance authorization and OOB/recovery access
Evidence handling rules appropriate for hardware security/fuse information
safety_requirements: Never burn, program, repair, unlock or otherwise change PCH fuses in this read-only test.
Stop before invocation if the selected mode can write, target identity is ambiguous or status semantics are not authoritative.
Preserve raw status, target identity and any error; do not reduce acceptance to an unqualified generic PASS banner.
Do not auto-retry, clear security evidence or attempt remediation after a mismatch.
agent_execution_scope: Check the supplied platform/tool/schema manifest and verify that the selected operation is read-only.
Guide evidence capture and correlate operator-supplied BIOS/KVM screenshots or transcripts with the exact PCH and decoded fields.
Report the observed values and comparison as Tool Result without asserting the manual action or formal verdict.
engineer_actions: Define whether 'PCH fuse', 'PCH security' and 'BIOS security status' refer to the same exact fields for this case.
Approve and perform the BIOS/diagnostic interaction and attest the captured display.
Apply the authoritative PASS definition and issue the formal verdict.

command_applicability.original_deepseek_command_fit: The generic instruction to run a vendor tool is not executable or safe until target, mode and status schema are pinned. It also fails to protect against permanent fuse programming.
command_applicability.command_recommendation: Retain only the owner-approved read-only BIOS diagnostic procedure. Do not invent an OS command or vendor syntax and do not substitute a generic security utility.
command_applicability.original_parameters_and_time_preserved: BIOS context, vendor-tool status check and 5/5-minute fields are preserved; no fuse write or remediation is added.

modernized_recommendation.status: OWNER DEFINITION REQUIRED; RETAIN READ-ONLY BIOS METHOD
modernized_recommendation.recommended_method: Use a signed diagnostic manifest that identifies every fuse/status field and decode table, then capture target-bound raw and rendered results from the BIOS/KVM session with a no-write attestation.
modernized_recommendation.applicable_platform: Only the exact motherboard/PCH stepping and BIOS/tool combination in the approved manifest.
modernized_recommendation.official_reference: Platform-owner and chipset-vendor fuse/security documentation; none was present in the repository.
modernized_recommendation.difference_from_original_method: Makes the ambiguous target and PASS semantics explicit and proves the check is read-only.
modernized_recommendation.coverage_difference: No reduction; all intended security/fuse fields must be evaluated, not only a generic banner.
modernized_recommendation.required_inputs: Field mapping, decode schema and qualified operator procedure.
modernized_recommendation.risks_limitations: Security fuses may be irreversible and sensitive; screenshots without target and decode context are insufficient.

project_override_considerations: A project may define its own approved fuse-field set and expected values, but that override must be explicit, target-specific and read-only. It does not alter the master source or authorize programming.
expected_evidence: Board/PCH/stepping/BIOS identity, diagnostic hash/version, read-only attestation and authorization
Authoritative field map, decode schema and expected PASS values
Operator-attributed BIOS/KVM entry and full raw/rendered fuse/security status tied to the target
No-write confirmation, BMC/SEL health, discrepancy analysis, Tool Result and separate engineer verdict

source_conflict_analysis.analysis: The item names a 'PCH fuse' check, the introductory instruction says PCH security, and the concrete step says BIOS security status, while the criterion only says 'status is pass.' These labels can cover different targets and no field/decode mapping resolves them, so owner clarification is required without inventing semantics.

blocked_analysis.analysis: The high-level read-only security inspection is understandable. The missing field map, tool and PASS definition are owner/readiness inputs; the explicitly BIOS/visual core is MANUAL ONLY, not permanently BLOCKED.

comparison_to_prior_reviews.deepseek: Retains the vendor-tool dependency but corrects the weak generic execution instruction and absent irreversible-fuse safety boundary.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.gpt_v2: Retains its read-only, identity, schema and operator gates but classifies the specified BIOS display interaction as MANUAL ONLY rather than PARTIAL.
comparison_to_prior_reviews.v3_1_improvement: Identifies the three inconsistent target labels as a source conflict and separates human observation from evidence analysis.

review_improvement: Prevents accidental fuse programming and false acceptance of a generic PASS string while preserving the source's BIOS-based inspection.
independent_technical_reasoning: A fuse-status check is safe only when exact fields and read-only behavior are established. Because the source's core occurs in BIOS and depends on human navigation/visual evidence, supplying a tool does not make the specified method automatically executable. The target-label mismatch is real but does not erase the identifiable inspection intent.
